expectations.evidence: Mix of abbreviated (_mu, q, sw, tb, rpm, lim), descriptive (retry_after, refill_rate, active_keys), and contextual (cutoff, deficit, elapsed). No over-reliance on generic names.

Comments reference real events ('2024-09 incident', 'Tried the threaded approach in Q1', 'old config before we moved to env-based'), explain WHY not WHAT, and include practical notes ('never return 0, causes tight loops'). No line-by-line commenting.
Functions range from 3-line peek() to 30+ line try_acquire(). Classes have different shapes. _BucketState dataclass placed between classes (organic placement).
CompositeLimiter validates inputs (raise ValueError), TokenBucket silently returns False for impossible requests, SlidingWindow doesn't validate at all. Mix of strategies.
MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS defined but unused (leftover), comment about 'old config', 'bumped from 3 to 5' showing parameter history, peek() deliberately skips refill (intentional design note).
Module docstring is practical/brief, class docstrings explain when to use (not obvious). No docstrings on reset(), peek() gets one-liner. No @param/@returns boilerplate.
